from pinneapple_neural.callbacks import PhysicsTrainerCallback
PhysicsTrainerCallback(PhysicsMonitor(..., model_fn=lambda m: m.net)).attach(trainer)
  • Checks. The monitor accepts any problem pp.validate takes: "darcy_2d", a zoo card, a PINN problem ({"pinn": "burgers_1d"}, PINN validation), a rollout, a tabular spec. level picks the checks. Each check's value is logged as physics/<check id>, plus physics/n_fail and physics/n_warn.
  • model_fn. Maps the framework's module to the network to validate, e.g. when a LightningModule or a Hugging Face model wraps it.
  • Early warning. For each watched check (watch=, default all numeric ones; a lower |value| is better), it counts consecutive checks in which the metric worsened while the loss fell. At patience it emits a PhysicsWarning that lands in monitor.alerts and in the trust card's training_alerts. With action="stop" it also stops training.
  • Training-time losses. pinneapple_analysis.uncertainty.residual_bound.ResidualLoss is a differentiable physics loss ‖f − A u‖² / ‖f‖² in the discretisation of the reference solver (sparse, PyTorch). The tests train with it.

docs.title: Results (from tests/test_training_callbacks.py, CPU)
docs.text:
A PhysicsNeMo FNO (2 layers, 6 modes) on 64 Darcy samples at 16 × 16, validated every 40 steps on 8 reference solutions of operator_benchmarks.darcy_2d, 400 steps, loss = relative data MSE + w × ResidualLoss:

Run Result w = 0.01, trained in Lightning and in a PhysicsNeMo loop identical physics metrics at all 10 checks (to 1e-5); no alert; relative L2 0.09, energy-norm error bound 0.44 w = 0.01, Hugging Face Trainer 10 checks logged through trainer.log; no alert w = −0.01 (sign error: the residual is maximised) alert at step 160 of 400 on the energy bound, the flux and the reference error; this is the earliest step every=40, patience=3 allows. With action="stop", training stops there (also in the HF Trainer).

Observed but not asserted in the tests: with w = 0 (data loss only), the monitor flags conservation.flux at step 200. The boundary-flux imbalance rises from 0.22 to 0.37 while the data loss keeps falling. This is the kind of drift the callback is for.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• A check costs one pp.validate call on the validation batch. For Darcy at level="quick" with 8 samples at 16 × 16 it takes about 13 ms; at standard, which adds the spectral and symmetry tests, about 28 ms. Choose every accordingly.
  • The rule needs the loss at each check. In the Hugging Face Trainer it is the latest logged loss, so set logging_steps no larger than every.
  • Identical metrics across frameworks require identical training: the same initial weights, batch order and optimiser. The HF Trainer shuffles and uses its own optimiser, so its run is checked for logging and stopping, not for equality.
  • pp.validate could not run a PhysicsNeMo FNO given a field without a channel axis: PhysicsNeMo raises ValueError, not RuntimeError. This is fixed here.

docs.title: A latent surrogate that says when not to trust it
docs.text:
A latent reduced-order model encodes the solver's fields in a few coordinates (POD), regresses those coordinates on the design parameters, and decodes. It answers in a fraction of a millisecond, and answers just as fast where it is wrong. TrustedLatentSurrogate (in pinneapple_neural.architectures.rom) adds three checks to every answer, calibrated on designs the latent model never saw, and hands the result to the library's TrustReport:

check what it measures calibrated how in the report error bound latent predictive spread (Gaussian-process std, or a bootstrap ensemble of latent regressors) scaled to the relative L2 error of the field normalised split-conformal: covers the true error with probability 1 - alpha for queries drawn like the calibration set not critical: above the tolerance → REVIEW design envelope mean distance to the k nearest training designs conformal p-value against the calibration designs critical: p < alpha_envelope → REJECT physics residual the discrete governing equations evaluated on the decoded field (a sparse mat-vec, no solve) 1 - alpha_residual conformal quantile of calibration residuals critical → REJECT

The envelope check exists because conformal coverage only holds while queries look like the calibration data; out there the spread itself can be overconfident. The physics residual is independent of the data: it sees errors that every member of an ensemble agrees on.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from pinneapple_neural.architectures.rom import ParametricPOD, TrustedLatentSurrogate

sur = TrustedLatentSurrogate(
    ParametricPOD(r=64, regressor="gpr", normalize=True),   # latent model; "rbf" uses a bootstrap ensemble
    alpha=0.1,                                              # 90 % error bound
    residual=lambda p, u: rel_residual(p, u),               # optional: ||L(p) u - f(p)|| / ||f(p)||
).fit(P_train, X_train, P_cal, X_cal)                       # calibration designs: never used for fitting

a = sur.assess(P_new, tol=0.02)        # X, error_bound, envelope_p, residual, decision per query
report = sur.trust_report(P_new[0], tol=0.02)
report.decisao, report.to_markdown()   # APPROVED / REVIEW / REJECT with the reasons

assess returns the same decision as the report: REJECT on an envelope or residual failure, REVIEW when the error bound exceeds the tolerance, APPROVED otherwise. A REVIEW or REJECT means "run the solver for this one", which is what a design loop or a digital twin should do with the answer.

docs.title: Experiment: every answer against the full solver
docs.text:
python examples/latent/trusted_latent_surrogate.py --seed 0 (also seeds 1 and 2). Full model: steady 2-D advection-diffusion-reaction of a Gaussian source on a 96 × 96 grid (upwind finite differences, sparse direct solve), four parameters (wind speed, direction, decay rate, source position). 150 training and 100 calibration designs from an envelope with a hole (a band of wind speeds and directions never simulated). Three test groups of 150: inside the envelope, inside the hole (inside the parameter box, so a box check passes them), and 5–30 % beyond the box in one parameter. Tolerance: 2 % relative L2 error. Mean of three seeds, [min, max] where it varies:

envelope hole beyond the box median / p95 relative error 0.84 % / 3.8 % 0.61 % / 1.4 % 4.9 % / 17 % nearest training design (baseline), median 17 % 20 % 31 % fraction with error > 2 % 15 % 2 % 90 % coverage of the 90 % error bound 0.92 [0.87, 0.96] 0.99 0.65 APPROVED / REVIEW / REJECT 58 / 39 / 3 % 71 / 28 / 0 % 6 / 18 / 76 % approved with error > 2 % 2.4 % 0.4 % 1.6 %

Detecting a wrong answer (error > 2 %) over all 450 queries, ROC AUC: error bound 0.980, physics residual 0.976, envelope p-value 0.943, box check 0.891. Spearman correlation with the true error: bound 0.95, residual 0.93.

As a gate, over the three seeds: the trust decision approved 607 answers, of which 20 (3.3 %) were wrong, the largest approved error being 1.2 %, 3.5 % and 5.3 % per seed. A box check approved the 900 in-box answers, of which 79 (8.8 %) were wrong, with largest approved errors of 7.4 % to 14.5 %.

Speed: full solve 45.6 ms; surrogate 0.71 ms per query in a batch (65 times faster), 2.5 ms per query with the three checks (18 times faster). A single query costs 11 ms (only 4 times faster) because scikit-learn's GP prediction has a fixed per-call overhead for each latent coordinate; batch the queries.

What the numbers say:

  • The latent model is genuinely useful here (0.8 % median error, 20 times better than the nearest design), and most of its failures are recognisable before anyone looks at the reference: the bound and the residual each rank wrong answers with AUC ≈ 0.98.
  • The hole turned out to be interpolable (0.6 % error), and the gate approved most of it: the envelope check flags distance, but the decision only rejects when the p-value is extreme, so the gate is not needlessly conservative.
  • Beyond the box the coverage of the bound drops to 0.65, which is why the envelope check is critical: it rejects three quarters of those queries.
  • The error bound is marginal over the calibration distribution, not conditional per query. With 100 calibration designs the coverage fluctuates by a few percent between seeds, and the approval rate inside the envelope varied from 33 % to 71 %: more calibration designs make both steadier.

docs.title: Uncertainty and sensitivity studies on any model
docs.text:
Two questions every surrogate (or solver) raises before anyone uses its numbers: how far can I trust this prediction? and which parameters actually control it? PINNeAPPle answers both on any model that maps an (n, d) array of inputs to (n, m) outputs: a pp.zoo model, an ONNX graph, a solver wrapper or a closed form.

import pinneapple as pp
from pinneapple_analysis.study_models import StudyModel

model = StudyModel.from_zoo("heatsink_forced_mlp", outputs=["r_base_k_w"])   # also from_onnx(bytes), builtin("ishigami")
X_cal, y_cal = model.reference("cal")                                         # the model's own calibration split
X_test, y_test = model.reference("test")                                      # held out: never used to calibrate

study = pp.conformal_study(y_cal[:, 0], model.predict(X_cal)[:, 0], y_test[:, 0], model.predict(X_test)[:, 0],
                           alpha=0.1, scale_cal=model.predict(X_cal)[:, 0], scale_test=model.predict(X_test)[:, 0])
print(study.coverage, study.coverage_ci)            # measured on the 900 test designs, with its Wilson interval

docs.title: Uncertainty (pp.uncertainty)
docs.text:
Question API Interval with a coverage guarantee, measured on held-out data conformal_study(y_cal, pred_cal, y_test, pred_test, alpha, scale_cal=, scale_test=, group_by=) Uncertain inputs with distributions distributions.as_space([...]): uniform, normal, truncnormal, lognormal (median, gsd), triangular Propagate them through the model propagate_space(fn, space, n, method="mc" / "lhs" / "sobol", limits=) (pp.propagate_uncertainty) Cheap moments and Sobol indices for a smooth model with few inputs polynomial_chaos(fn, space, degree) with its leave-one-out Q2 Is this input inside the data the model learned from? ApplicabilityDomain.fit(X_ref, names, bounds).assess(X): inside / sparse / outside Which cases need the high-fidelity solver? route_cases(status, pred, lower, upper, tolerance=, limits=) + routing_summary

Conformal intervals are valid on average over data like the calibration data. Two reports keep that honest: the reliability list (measured coverage at several nominal levels) and the per-group coverage (group_by= an input or the prediction), which shows where a constant-width interval under-covers. Normalised scores (a scale per point: the prediction itself for a relative error, an ensemble spread) make the width follow the error.

The applicability gate uses the declared validity range (a model card's) and the k-nearest-neighbour distance in standardised inputs: a point is sparse when its 5th neighbour is farther than for 99 % of the reference points themselves (a hole in the data inside the range). The routing rule sends a case to the high-fidelity solver when it is outside or sparse, when its interval is wider than the tolerance the decision needs, or when its interval contains a decision limit.

docs.title: Sensitivity (pp.sensitivity)
docs.text:
Question API Share of output variance per input, with confidence intervals sobol_indices(fn, space, n, second_order=True) (pp.sobol_indices) Same, from runs done elsewhere (OpenFOAM, CalculiX, a campaign) saltelli_design(space, n, seed=) → run → sobol_from_runs(space, n, run_ids, Y, seed=) From an existing dataset, no designed experiment first_order_given_data(X, y) Cheap screening of many inputs morris(fn, space, r): mu*, sigma, r (d + 1) evaluations Shape of each effect, interactions effect_curves(fn, space): partial dependence + ICE Local gradient local_derivatives(fn, x0, torch_fn=): autodiff for torch models, central differences otherwise Which inputs can be fixed? freeze_recommendation(indices, threshold) and the direct check verify_freeze(fn, space, frozen)

The estimators are Saltelli (2010) for first order, Jansen (1999) for total and Saltelli (2002) for second order, with percentile-bootstrap intervals. tests/test_sensitivity.py checks them against the exact indices of the Ishigami and Sobol' G functions (pinneapple_analysis.sensitivity.testfunctions). An input is recommended for freezing only when the upper bound of its total index is below the threshold for every output; an estimate below the threshold with a wider interval is reported as inconclusive (more samples needed), never as freezable.

docs.title: Apps
docs.text:
• Engineering Sensitivity Lab (sensitivity.pinneapple.org): Sobol, Morris, effect curves, derivatives and the freeze recommendation for a model, solver runs or a dataset.
  • Engineering Uncertainty Lab (uncertainty.pinneapple.org): intervals, applicability alerts, the routing rule and propagation for a model and its data.

docs.title: Engineering Uncertainty Lab
docs.text:
Know when a prediction is reliable, and when the case must go to the high-fidelity solver. Day 15 of the apps series: https://uncertainty.pinneapple.org (source: apps/uncertainty_lab).

Pick a model (a pp.zoo model or an uploaded ONNX graph), its reference data, the cases you want to decide on, the uncertain inputs and the decision limits. The lab returns:

  • split-conformal intervals with their coverage measured on held-out data (Wilson interval, reliability across levels, coverage per region and per applicability gate; the raw ensemble interval for comparison when the model has one);
  • applicability alerts: outside the validity range, or inside it where the reference data are sparse;
  • a routing rule per case (surrogate or high-fidelity solver, with the reasons), checked against the heat-sink physics engine where the library has it;
  • propagation of uncertain inputs (Monte Carlo, Latin hypercube, Sobol; polynomial chaos when cheap), with the probability of meeting the limits with and without the model's own error.

On the heat-sink example the 90 % intervals cover 91.0 % (95 % CI 89.0–92.7 %) of the 900 held-out designs. Of eleven screened designs, the only one whose engine value falls outside its interval is the corner of the design space, which the gate flags as sparse and routes to the solver. On the airfoil example the model's own ensemble interval covers 75 % of held-out OpenFOAM runs at a 90 % nominal level; the conformal interval on the same spread covers 88 %.

Everything shown comes from one library call, pp.uncertainty.uncertainty_study (see Uncertainty and sensitivity studies on any model). Limits, methods and the API are in the app README.

docs.title: Red team / blue team for the validation checks
docs.text:
The check power matrix measures the checks against a fixed list of defects, which only shows that they catch the defects someone already thought of. The arena (pinneapple_analysis.validation.arena, issue #707) adds an adversary. A red team searches for wrong outputs that pass every check (escapes) and for correct outputs that fail (false alarms). A blue team then calibrates the checks with a stated false-alarm rate and strengthens them until every stored escape is caught. Escapes and false alarms are stored as regression cases, and CI replays them.

import pinneapple as pp

rep = pp.validate.arena("darcy_2d", budget="small", alpha=0.05)      # = arena.run_arena(...)
print(rep.to_markdown())        # per round: escapes, false alarms, mutation score, ROC/AUC, min. detectable magnitude
assert rep.passed, rep.failures()
rep.save_cases("cases/darcy_2d.json")

pinneapple check --arena-cases                    # replay the cases shipped with the library
pinneapple check --arena-cases cases/*.json       # or your own; exit 1 on a regression
python examples/validation_arena/run_arena.py     # full size on Darcy 2-D and Burgers 1-D

docs.title: Red team
docs.text:
• Mutation operators. These are the fault library of #697 (bias, scale, smoothing, noise, wrong boundary values, sign flips, out-of-range use, stale models) applied at every magnitude. The mutation score is the share of the mutants that matter (true relative error ≥ 10 %) which the defence rejects. This is the test-adequacy measure of mutation testing for deep learning (DeepCrime, Humbatova et al. 2021; MuFF, arXiv:2501.09846), with the checks as the tests. A mutant that matters and passes is an escape.
  • Search-based evasion. Each generator is a parametrised family of outputs. The search maximises the true error against the reference solver while every check stays under its threshold, using differential evolution (SciPy), CMA-ES (written from Hansen's tutorial, arXiv:1604.00772) or finite-difference L-BFGS-B (method=).
  • Physics-consistent attacks. These outputs solve a nearby problem exactly, so the residual stays small:
  • Darcy: a smooth change of log a (coefficient_field) or of f (source_field);
  • Burgers: another viscosity (viscosity), the exact initial condition followed by the evolution of a smoothed one (hard_ic_evolution, what a hard-constrained PINN with spectral bias returns), or rescaled time (time_warp).
  • False-alarm search. The search runs over correct cases from the verified solvers, with coefficient contrast, feature size, amplitude, viscosity and solver resolution varied inside the training envelope, and maximises the largest margin of the defence. The result is the most suspicious-looking correct case, which counts as a false alarm when it is rejected.

docs.title: Blue team
docs.text:
• Calibrated combined test. The clean calibration cases are split in two halves, A and B. Each check's scale s_j is its split-conformal quantile on A (pinneapple_analysis.uncertainty.conformal.conformal_quantile), with a floor of 1 % of its own tolerance. The combined statistic is T = max_j value_j / s_j, and its threshold is the split-conformal quantile of T on B. The probability that a new clean case is rejected by any check is then at most alpha_cal (Vovk et al. 2005; Angelopoulos & Bates, arXiv:2107.07511). This is the family-wise rate, so false alarms do not grow with the number of checks.
  • alpha_cal = safety × alpha, with safety = 0.5 by default, so that the rate measured on a finite held-out set stays under the stated alpha.
  • The guarantee needs ceil((n_B + 1)(1 - alpha_cal)) ≤ n_B, and Defence.alpha_guaranteed reports whether that holds.
  • Hardening. Stored false alarms are correct cases, so the threshold is raised just above them; this can only lower the false-alarm rate. While a stored escape still passes, the blue team adds the check from check_library(problem) that rejects the most remaining escapes after recalibration. The log records what was added and why.
  • Regression cases. Every escape and false alarm is saved with its case seed, variation, generator and parameters, together with the hardened thresholds. pinneapple check --arena-cases regenerates each case and requires escapes to be rejected and false alarms to pass.

docs.title: Results (seed 0, alpha = 0.01, 2 rounds, full budget)
docs.text:
Full budget: 400 clean calibration cases, 300 held-out clean cases, 3 base cases × 160 evaluations per generator, and 4 random fields × 80 evaluations for the false-alarm search. Regenerate with python examples/validation_arena/run_arena.py --rounds 2.

Darcy 2-D Burgers 1-D round-0 defence (hand-set tolerances) FD residual, boundary condition, bounds, training envelope FD residual, initial condition, bounds, training envelope escapes found at round 0 (true error ≥ 10 %, every check passes) 15 16 worst escape coefficient_field: 87 % true error time_warp (s = 0.5): 50 % true error mutation score, before → after 67.3 % → 100 % (419 mutants) 75.5 % → 100 % (351 mutants) held-out false-alarm rate, hand tolerances → combined test 1.33 % → 0.00 % (0.67 % after round 1) 0.00 % → 1.00 % worst false alarm (most suspicious correct case) margin −0.11, accepted margin −0.03, accepted check added by the blue team conservative residual on the solver stencil one-step re-integration residual stored escapes rejected after blue 15/15 16/16 escapes ≥ 10 % found at round 1 against the hardened defence 0 (largest accepted error 4.9 %) 0

How to read these results:

  • Round 0 shows that the default checks have real blind spots. A Darcy output solved for the wrong permeability field, or a Burgers solution at the wrong time, has a small finite-difference residual and the right boundary or initial condition. Every check accepts it, yet it is wrong by 50-87 %.
  • The strengthened checks close these gaps because they use the solver's own discretisation.
  • No correct case was rejected by the hand-set tolerances in the search. The held-out set did contain 4 correct Darcy cases (out of 300) that the hand-set tolerances flag.
  • The calibrated test states its rate:
  • Darcy stays under 1 % with a margin.
  • Burgers is at the bound (3 of 300). Its one-step residual is calibrated on correct cases solved at finer resolution, so the tail is real.

The report also lists, for every check and fault, the detection rate, the false-alarm rate, the ROC AUC over fault magnitude and the minimal detectable magnitude, before and after the round.

docs.title: External models
docs.text: audit_model(problem, predict) runs any model through the hardened defence shipped with the library and compares each output with the reference solver. predict(inputs, params) returns the field on the problem's grid (Darcy a → u on 32 × 32 cells, Burgers u0 → u(t, x)). The result lists the escapes (wrong outputs the defence accepts) and the accurate outputs it rejects. This is the hook for the FNO and MeshGraphNet models of the PhysicsNeMo trust experiment: wrap their inference as predict (PhysicsNeMo is not a dependency of PINNeAPPle, so this is not run in CI).

docs.title: Scope and limits
docs.text:
• Two problems with verified solvers. A check is only as strong as the discretisation it shares with the reference: the conservative residual flags correct solutions computed on a different grid at the level of the discretisation error, which is why it is calibrated rather than set to round-off.
  • The evasion search is local to its budget. "No escape found" means none within the stated evaluations, not none at all; the report says which.
  • The data-level arena (datasets rather than single outputs) is measured by the fault-injection matrix with the dataset checks; the conformal calibration covers the case-level checks.

docs.title: Validation gallery: one worked example per model family and per physics
docs.text:
examples/validation/ shows how to validate your kind of model on your kind of physics. Every example has the same structure:

  1. Train or load the model, with data from the library's reference solvers or the zoo.
  2. Run pp.validate.
  3. Read the trust card. validation.gallery.conclude writes report.json, trust_card.json, report.sarif and failure.json to examples/_out/validation/<example>/.
  4. Run pinneapple check in CI.
  5. See one real failure the checks catch, on a broken variant of the same model.

Everything runs on a CPU. CI runs the whole gallery at smoke size (.github/workflows/validation-gallery.yml; under 3 minutes on a 4-core machine) and fails if an example stops catching its failure. Run one example with python examples/validation/<file>.py [--full].

examples/validation/pinneapple-check.toml runs two of the models (12 and the zoo model of 07) through pinneapple check with the same relations and range checks. The other examples write report.sarif, which the GitHub Action uploads to code scanning.

docs.title: Library additions made for the gallery
docs.text:
• pp.validate(sampler, {"generative": {...}}). A generative model is a sampler n -> {column: array}. Its samples are audited like a dataset: every sample against the PDE, diversity (mode collapse) and memorisation (generated samples that copy training samples).
  • Rollouts of state vectors (ndim = 0, e.g. particle systems or ROM coefficients) and user invariants ("invariants": {name: f(traj, ndim)}) in pp.validate rollout specs.
  • numerical_solvers.reaction_diffusion.ReactionDiffusion1D: Allen–Cahn and Fisher–KPP with ETDRK4. It is checked against the stationary tanh interface and the Bramson-corrected KPP front speed.
  • pinneapple_neural.utils.fit_supervised: a minimal Adam loop on (x, y) tensors.

docs.title: Honest results
docs.text:
• The FNO of example 02 is rejected at smoke size. Its net boundary flux misses the source by 29 %, it has too much high-wavenumber energy and it breaks the reflection symmetry by 10 %. The gallery reports that rather than tuning it away; the envelope failure is caught regardless.
  • Spectrum floor. On Allen–Cahn, every network "failed" rollout.spectrum until the band was restricted to shells with energy above 1e-6 of the peak (amplitudes above 0.1 %). Below that the reference holds only round-off. This is now the default of spectral_drift.
  • Data loss and physics disagree. In example 09 the neural ODE fits the training data better than the Hamiltonian network (loss 0.011 vs 0.048) and still drifts in energy. In example 12 the MLP passes a loose error check on some test sets while breaking the scaling laws.
  • Two solvers were not used, because they failed a sanity check:
  • generate_magnetic_flux_leakage_synthetic: the peak leakage signal is not monotonic in defect depth and changes with the grid (36 × 14, 72 × 28, 144 × 56).
  • eddy_current_fdm at ω = 0: the on-axis field of a coil was a fraction of the closed-form current-loop field. The solver was right; annular_current_source normalised the density by the nominal band area, so the current it injected depended on how the band fell on the grid. It now injects exactly N·I, and the on-axis field matches the loop formula (tests/test_em_core.py). Examples 11 and 08 still use the Darcy operator and the heat plate.
  • Smoke sizes are small. The FNO and DeepONet numbers (horizons, spectra) change with training length; the tests assert that each failure is caught and that the good model does not fail the same check, not the exact values.

docs.title: Validation methods reference
docs.text:
This page lists every check that PINNeAPPle's validation layer runs on a result, a model or a dataset. For each one it says:

  • what the check detects;
  • what it assumes;
  • its default threshold and where to change it;
  • the reference it follows;
  • what it cannot detect.

It covers the existing modules: pinneapple check, pp.trust_card, pinneapple_analysis.validation, pinneapple_analysis.uncertainty, pinneapple_analysis.verification, pinneapple_veriphysics, the physics audit (pinneapple_physics.physics_audit), conservation projections, and the zoo query gate.

A check passing is evidence, not proof. Every check here can be passed by a wrong result that happens to satisfy what the check measures. Section 10 explains how to measure the power of a check (mutation testing, metamorphic relations, adversarial search). The limitations listed for each check are the known ones. If you find a new one, add it here.

docs.title: 1. Status and decision vocabulary
docs.text:
The modules grew separately and use different words for the same outcomes. Until one schema exists (#696, #706), use this table to read them consistently.

Unified status pinneapple check trust_card TrustReport physics audit monitor zoo query gate veriphysics map pass (no finding) PASS supports OK pass PASS warn warning (not used) (not used) WARN warn INFO fail error FAIL contradicts ALARM (critical or persistent) fail FAIL not-applicable / not run (rule not applicable, PC002 if nothing ran) N/A not_run (check absent) (check absent) NOT_RUN

The deploy decisions APPROVED / REVIEW / REJECT (TrustReport.decisao, FieldTrustCard.decision, pp.zoo.validate(...).decisao) follow fixed rules:

  • any failed critical check gives REJECT;
  • any other failure gives REVIEW;
  • coverage (the fraction of checks that ran) below min_coverage, default 0.6 (0.5 for trust_card), gives REVIEW;
  • a weighted score below min_score (default 0.8) gives REVIEW;
  • otherwise the decision is APPROVED.

A check that could not run is never counted as a pass. It lowers coverage.

Stable check IDs: pinneapple check rules are PC001 to PC901 (pinneapple_check.rules.RULES), grouped by hundreds (--select PC1 picks every conservation rule). The zoo query gate reuses these IDs: PC601, PC602, PC402, PC403, PC302.

docs.title: 2. pinneapple check (results and models in CI)
docs.text:
Guide: Physics checks in CI. Every tolerance is relative and dimensionless. You can override each one per target under tolerances (pinneapple_check.config.DEFAULT_TOLERANCES).

Rule Detects Default Assumes / limitations PC101 mass net boundary volume flux / total absolute boundary flux 1e-3 incompressible or steady flow. On OpenFOAM cases it uses phi when written (exact to solver tolerance), otherwise the interpolated face velocity, which carries interpolation error. A leak that is balanced elsewhere on the boundary is invisible. PC102 divergence RMS(div u) / RMS(sum of abs velocity gradients) 1e-2 (stored), 5e-2 (model) the discrete operator (FV, FD or least squares) has its own truncation error. On coarse meshes the value is dominated by it. PC103 energy net boundary heat flow plus source / total absolute heat flow 1e-2 steady conduction with constant k. Convection and radiation terms are not included. PC104 momentum resultant of boundary tractions plus body force / total traction 1e-2 static linear elasticity, plane strain in 2-D. PC105 conserved total max |Q(t) - Q(t0)| / |Q(t0)| 1e-3 a closed domain, or a declared boundary-flux column. Q(t0) = 0 makes the ratio undefined. PC201/PC202 BC/IC max |value - declared| / field scale 1e-3 / 1e-2 Dirichlet values only. Neumann conditions are checked through the balances. PC203 wall velocity max |U| on wall patches / velocity scale 1e-6 a moving wall must be declared. PC301/PC302 residual RMS residual / RMS of the sum of absolute terms 5e-2 the ratio is 0 when the equation holds, near 1 when the terms do not balance. Discretisation error makes it non-zero on coarse grids, which is why the default is loose. A small residual does not mean a small error: the residual does not see a wrong boundary condition or a wrong parameter that the PDE still satisfies. On point clouds the weighted quadratic fit gives first-order second derivatives (second order on tensor-product grids), so the residual of an exact solution falls more slowly with density there. PC401/PC402/PC403 values outside declared bounds; physically impossible values (T, rho at or below 0, fractions outside [0, 1], k, epsilon, omega, nut below 0); NaN/Inf 0 slack (1e-6 on fractions) PC402 infers the quantity from the field name and unit. PC501–PC504 units unit mismatch or missing unit; magnitudes implausible for the unit; parameters of the wrong dimension none (exact) units must be written in the file or declared. PC601/PC602 OOD query outside the training box; query inside the box but more than 3 typical spacings from every training sample (standardised) none box bounds miss correlated inputs. A query inside the box can still be far from the data manifold, and PC602 only partly covers this. PC701/PC702 regression relative L2 against a stored reference; QoI relative/absolute tolerance 1e-2 the reference must have been produced by a trusted run. PC801–PC804 integrity SHA-256 manifest, signatures, unsafe pickles, untracked files none (exact) PC901 catalog the method is not validated in pinneapple_catalog none

docs.title: 3. Trust card of a field on a grid (pp.trust_card)
docs.text:
pinneapple_analysis.trust.field_card runs on a tensor-product grid and uses NumPy only. Tolerances are in DEFAULT_TOLERANCES and can be overridden with tolerances={...}.

Check Measures Default Reference / limitations finite values (critical) NaN or Inf anywhere 0 a non-finite field stops the card: REJECT. PDE residual (critical) laplace(u) = f or u_t = alpha laplace(u) + f, three-point finite differences on the interior. RMS residual / RMS of the sum of absolute terms. 0.05 Second order on uniform grids. The tests check order 2.00 on uniform and stretched grids against exact Laplace, Poisson and heat solutions. The scale has a floor at the round-off of the stencil, so exactly harmonic linear fields pass (#708). It needs 4 or more points per axis and only checks interior points. boundary conditions (critical) max |u - g| / range of u on each named face 0.02 Dirichlet only. conservation |net boundary flux of grad u - integral of f| / total absolute flux (divergence theorem) 0.05 Steady problems only. Uses second-order one-sided boundary gradients and trapezoidal quadrature, so it needs 3 or more points per axis. A field with the right total flux but the wrong distribution passes. maximum principle interior overshoot beyond the boundary range / range of u 0.01 Laplace without a source only. reference (critical) relative L2 against an array or a closed form 0.05 A zero reference makes the ratio meaningless. Give an absolute comparison instead. applicability (OOD) fraction of query points inside train_bounds 1.0 Box bounds only.

pinneapple_analysis.trust.TrustGate scores one prediction of a trained model:

  • OOD: each query point gets the chi-squared p-value of its Mahalanobis distance to the training coordinates. The score is the fraction of points with p >= ood_level (default 0.01) (#713). fit_from_bounds treats a box as a Gaussian with the box variance; in 6 or more dimensions the corners of the training box fall outside the 99 % region.
  • Residual: 1 / (1 + RMS residual). This depends on the units of the residual, so compare it only between models of the same problem.
  • Ensemble: 1 / (1 + mean relative std).

trust_report.from_trust_score turns these scores into checks with a design threshold of 0.7.

docs.title: 4. Model validation (pinneapple_analysis.validation)
docs.text:
PhysicsValidator evaluates a model (with autograd) at sampled points. Each check defaults to tolerance=1e-3.

  • ConservationCheck (mass, energy, custom integrals): Monte Carlo integration. The estimate has O(n^-1/2) sampling noise, so n_points must be large enough that the noise is below the tolerance.
  • BoundaryCheck (Dirichlet, Neumann, periodic).
  • SymmetryCheck (reflection, 2-D rotation): max |u(Sx) - s u(x)|. Use it only when the problem, including its boundary conditions and sources, has the symmetry.
  • compare_to_analytical / validate_against_solver: RMSE, relative L2 and max error against a closed form or solver data.

Limitation: sampled checks can miss narrow features such as boundary layers or shocks. Use the grid checks in sections 2 and 3 on a resolved field when such features matter.

docs.title: 5. Uncertainty (pinneapple_analysis.uncertainty)
docs.text: Method What it guarantees or measures Assumptions / limitations ConformalPredictor (split conformal; Vovk et al. 2005, Angelopoulos and Bates 2022) marginal coverage of at least 1 - alpha in finite samples. The quantile is the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th order statistic, never interpolated. A Monte Carlo check with n_cal = 20 gives 0.902 for alpha = 0.1, inside [0.90, 0.948]. Exchangeable calibration and test data. Coverage is marginal, not conditional on x. The score is the L-infinity residual over outputs, so coverage is joint across outputs. The guarantee does not survive distribution shift: check drift. QuantileHead / QuantileLoss (pinball loss; Koenker and Bassett 1978) learned conditional quantiles No coverage guarantee without conformal calibration (CQR; Romano, Patterson and Candès 2019). Quantiles can cross. CalibrationMetrics (Kuleshov et al. 2018) ECE of the PIT of standardised residuals against the uniform distribution; coverage of Gaussian intervals; NLL; sharpness Gaussian predictive distribution. Multi-output metrics are element-wise averages (#715). ECE is below 0.01 for a calibrated model and about 0.1 when the std is off by a factor of 2. Default review tolerances in veriphysics: ECE 0.10, coverage within 0.05. assess_drift (DriftThresholds) ok / review / retrain from nRMSE (0.2 / 0.5), bias z-test (3 sigma), coverage z-test (3 sigma), per-feature KS with Bonferroni (alpha 0.01), out-of-range fraction (0.01 / 0.10), Mann-Kendall trend (alpha 0.01) Tests assume independent residuals. Autocorrelated time series inflate the false-alarm rate. propagate (tolerances) Monte Carlo propagation of input tolerances, Wilson intervals on pass fractions The input distribution (uniform or normal) is an assumption you supply. crps_gaussian / crps_ensemble (Gneiting et al. 2005; Gneiting and Raftery 2007; Ferro 2014) proper scores of a predictive distribution crps_gaussian matches the closed form exactly. fair=True is unbiased for small ensembles: with 5 members, the average over 20 000 draws is 0.4218 against the exact 0.4216, while the plain version gives 0.532. block_bootstrap / group_bootstrap (Künsch 1989) percentile intervals of a statistic of dependent data Percentile intervals undercover in small or strongly dependent samples. In a Monte Carlo test of the mean, iid data with n = 100 gave 0.93 coverage at a nominal 0.95. An AR(1) series with coefficient 0.9, n = 1200 and blocks of 60 gave 0.90. Choose blocks several correlation times long, and read the interval as approximate. ensembles, MC dropout, decomposition, posterior metrics, resampling, reachability epistemic spread, aleatoric/epistemic split (law of total variance), bootstrap intervals, reachable sets Ensemble spread is not calibrated by itself: calibrate it against a reference (veriphysics calibration_against_reference) or with conformal prediction.

docs.title: 6. Solution and code verification (pinneapple_analysis.verification)
docs.text:
• richardson_extrapolate / mesh_independence_study (Roache 1994; Celik et al. 2008). These compute the observed order, the Richardson value, GCI_fine and GCI_coarse with Fs = 1.25, and the asymptotic ratio GCI_coarse / (r^p GCI_fine), which is near 1 in the asymptotic range (tolerance 0.10).
  • Non-constant refinement ratios use Celik's fixed-point iteration (#710). The tests reproduce Celik et al. (2008) Table 1: p = 1.53, phi_ext = 6.1685, GCI_fine = 2.17 %.
  • Ratios inferred from resolution counts assume h ~ 1/N in one dimension. For cell counts in D dimensions, pass r = (N_fine/N_medium)^(1/D) explicitly.
  • Oscillatory convergence gives a warning. The GCI is then not a reliable error band.
  • Array-valued quantities use L2 norms of the differences.
  • Manufactured solutions (Roache 2002; Salari and Knupp 2000). These are in tests/test_manufactured_solutions.py. Code verification means the observed order matches the scheme's formal order on a solution chosen in advance.
  • dimensional_analysis: unit consistency and Buckingham Pi groups.
  • geometry_ood_guardrail: z-scored geometry descriptors against a reference set.
  • physics_confidence_score: a bounded combination of calibration, convergence and residual evidence. The weights are design choices, not a standard.
  • provenance: hashes of the inputs of a run.

docs.title: 7. Veriphysics applicability and robustness (pinneapple_veriphysics)
docs.text:
The applicability map sorts every claim into three tiers:

  • VERIFIED: a check measured it in this run;
  • INFERRED: plausible, but not measured;
  • UNSUPPORTED: no evidence; do not use the surrogate there.

It also answers an eight-item review checklist. The tolerances are reviewer aids, not standards, and can be replaced per request (Tolerances):

  • training plateau: below 5 % change over the last 10 % of epochs;
  • ensemble and parameter-shift spread: 0.10;
  • ECE: 0.10;
  • coverage: within 0.05.

The robustness studies are:

  • ensembles over seeds;
  • extrapolation shells at 10, 25 and 50 % beyond the training box;
  • loss-weight sensitivity (x0.25 and x4);
  • parameter shifts (10 and 30 %);
  • calibration against a reference;
  • coverage of the boundary and initial conditions.

A small spread under these perturbations shows stability, not correctness: an ensemble can agree on a wrong answer.

docs.title: 8. Physics audit monitor and conservation projections (pinneapple_physics)
docs.text:
physics_audit.monitor.PhysicsValidityMonitor runs residual, conservation, bounds, boundary, constitutive, invariant and envelope checks on every prediction. A failed check gives WARN. A failed critical check, a failure that persists for persistence cases in a row (default 3), or a residual whose EWMA reaches 3x its baseline gives ALARM.

  • Conservation and invariant checks are relative to the expected value. When the expected value is zero (net charge, net momentum of a closed system), give abs_tol (#711).
  • boundary_check scales the mismatch by the larger of the RMS of the condition and the RMS of the prediction, so homogeneous conditions can pass (#711).

pinneapple_physics.conservation.project_integral enforces a weighted integral exactly, with additive, multiplicative or positive modes. It guarantees the total, not the local balance: a projected field can still violate the PDE locally.

docs.title: 9. Zoo query gate (pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks)
docs.text:
Each query is checked for:

  • the validity range (PC601);
  • sparse training regions (PC602);
  • non-finite or unphysical outputs (PC403, PC402);
  • ensemble agreement against its held-out level;
  • the model's physics residual at the query (PC302).

Any failing check gives fail, any warning gives warn, otherwise the verdict is pass. Design constraints are reported but never enter the verdict. The noise floor is 0.2 % of the output range. pp.zoo.validate reproduces the card metrics on the model as a whole.

docs.title: 10. How good are the checks? Credibility, check power and attacks
Credibility frameworks
docs.text:
ASME V&V 40-2018 (Assessing Credibility of Computational Modeling through Verification and Validation: Application to Medical Devices) and NASA-STD-7009A (Standard for Models and Simulations, 2016) do not prescribe thresholds. They ask that the rigour of each credibility factor scales with the model risk, which combines the influence of the model on the decision and the consequence of a wrong decision, within a stated context of use. The factors are code verification, solution verification, validation against references, uncertainty and applicability.

The checks above map to those factors:

Credibility factor Checks code verification manufactured solutions, solver order tests solution verification GCI, residual checks validation reference, regression, field metrics uncertainty section 5 applicability OOD, envelope, extrapolation shells

The default thresholds here are engineering defaults for a low-to-medium-risk context. For a high-risk context of use, tighten them and require more factors to be VERIFIED. Do not loosen them to get a pass. See also Oberkampf and Roy (2010), Verification and Validation in Scientific Computing.

docs.title: Mutation testing: measuring check adequacy
docs.text:
A check that never fails is not evidence. Mutation testing injects known faults and counts how many each check catches; the mutation score measures how adequate the checks are. Faults can be injected into the model (weights, scaling, sign flips) or into the data (drift, leakage, units). Relevant work:

  • DeepCrime (Humbatova, Jahangirova and Tonella, ISSTA 2021): mutation operators derived from real deep-learning faults.
  • MuFF (arXiv:2501.09846): stable post-training mutants.

docs.title: Metamorphic relations
docs.text:
When no oracle exists, check relations that must hold between runs: symmetry of the inputs, scaling laws, superposition for linear problems, refinement consistency. Relevant work:

  • Chen, Cheung and Yiu (1998), Metamorphic testing: a new approach for generating next test cases, HKUST-CS98-01;
  • Segura et al. (2016), A survey on metamorphic testing, IEEE TSE;
  • METTLE (arXiv:1807.10453).

The symmetry check in section 4 is a metamorphic relation.

docs.title: Adversarial robustness of neural operators
docs.text:
Small input perturbations can make neural-operator errors grow by orders of magnitude while the outputs stay plausible:

  • Adesoji and Chen (2022, arXiv:2204.04259) show this for FNO on Burgers, Darcy and Navier-Stokes;
  • a 2026 study (arXiv:2604.13316) reports accuracy losses of several orders of magnitude when fewer than 1 % of the inputs are perturbed.

No check on this page searches for such perturbations. A pass is evidence only for the inputs that were checked.

docs.title: Red team / blue team arena
docs.text: Issue #707 proposes an arena, implemented separately. Generators search for wrong-but-plausible cases that escape the checks and for correct cases that raise false alarms. The checks are then hardened, and their thresholds calibrated with a stated false-alarm rate. When it lands, its detection and false-alarm rates per check are the measured power of the methods on this page.

docs.title: Simulation Workflow Runner: campaigns as traceable, resumable workflows
docs.text: The Workflow Runner (day 27, runner.pinneapple.org) runs a simulation campaign as a DAG of steps per case. It records what happened to every step, picks up where an interrupted campaign stopped, reuses steps whose inputs did not change, and returns the finished runs as a training dataset. It orchestrates the tools you already have (OpenFOAM, CalculiX, Python, Docker, Slurm); it does not replace them.

docs.title: From cases to a dataset
docs.text:
1. Cases. A table with one row per case, as CSV, Parquet, HDF5 or JSON. A Campaign Planner export works as it is, including its .contract.json sidecar. On the public server the columns must be the template's parameters, inside its ranges.
  2. Template. The steps run for each case and their dependencies:
  3. slab heating: the exact solution of transient conduction, in Python;
  4. cantilever beam: a CalculiX deck from calculix.study.FEModel, then ccx, then a comparison with beam theory;
  5. lid-driven cavity: OpenFOAM's icoFoam on the tutorial case with edited dictionaries.
  6. Executor. Where the commands run: this server, Docker (self-hosted), or Slurm. On the public server, the Slurm executor only writes the sbatch scripts.
  7. Run. Each step has a state, attempts, wall time, outputs and a log. A failed step cancels only the steps that need it. Resume continues an interrupted or failed run. Run again starts a new run and reuses every step whose content hash is unchanged.
  8. Dataset. The parameters and outputs of every case, as CSV, Parquet, HDF5 or JSON, with a DatasetSpec. The spec records columns with units and roles, the file's SHA-256, and the run step behind each row.

docs.title: View a solver step's result in 3-D
docs.text:
A finished CalculiX or OpenFOAM step has a View result in 3-D button, a check before its numbers are used. It shows the mesh, the selected field and, for CalculiX, the deformed shape with a scale factor. The regions where the case defines its boundary conditions and loads are marked:

  • CalculiX: the *BOUNDARY, *CLOAD and *DLOAD sets of the deck;
  • OpenFOAM: the patches, with their conditions from the first time directory.

Large meshes are decimated above 250 k triangles (RUNNER_VIEW_MAX_FACES, from the size guide in the studio page). In Python: pinneapple_tools.visualization.studio.solver_view.solver_result_view(step_folder).

docs.title: The same engine in Python
docs.text:
from pinneapple_core.workflows import Step, Workflow, WorkflowRunner, TEMPLATES, dataset_from_run

runner = WorkflowRunner("work/runner")
t = TEMPLATES["slab_heat"]
cases = t.example_cases(20)                       # or read_cases("campaign.parquet")
run = runner.run(t.workflow(cases, max_parallel=4))
runner.run(run_id=run["id"])                      # resume (no-op when everything finished)
spec, path = dataset_from_run(runner, run["id"], cases, output_step="solve", path="slab.parquet")

wf = Workflow("beam", [
    Step("mesh", "command", {"argv": ["gmsh", "-3", "beam.geo", "-o", "beam.inp"]}, inputs=["beam.geo"]),
    Step("solve", "calculix", {"inp_from": "mesh", "job": "beam"}, needs=["mesh"], retries=1,
         executor="slurm", executor_options={"partition": "cpu", "ntasks": 8, "dry_run": True}),
])

New step kinds and executors plug in with register_adapter and register_executor (see the app README). This is how the Engineering GUI Agent adds GUI-driven steps.

docs.title: What was checked
docs.text:
• Skip-done, resume, retries. Tests in tests/pinneapple_core/test_workflows.py cover:
  • a rerun with unchanged content runs nothing;
  • changing one step's parameter reruns it and everything downstream;
  • a crash mid-run is resumed without redoing finished steps;
  • retries recover from transient failures;
  • cancel kills a running command.
  • Slurm. The generated script carries the partition, tasks, memory, account, time limit, modules and the srun line (dry run, tested).
  • CalculiX template. With CalculiX 2.21, the C3D8I tip deflection is 0.993 to 1.007 of Euler-Bernoulli over the six example beams. The test asserts within 2 % whenever ccx is installed.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Public server: built-in templates only, with numeric case values checked against the template's ranges. Self-hosting (RUNNER_SELF_HOSTED=1) enables custom commands, scripts and Docker steps. Only do that behind your own login.
  • Solvers. The public image has no OpenFOAM or CalculiX. Those templates show "needs solver" there instead of pretending.
  • OpenFOAM environment. OpenFOAM steps source the step's bashrc, else FOAM_BASHRC, else the first installation found in /usr/share/openfoam, /usr/lib/openfoam/openfoam*, /opt/openfoam* or /opt/OpenFOAM-*, unless the environment is loaded already (WM_PROJECT_DIR set).
  • Skip-done hashes only what a step declares. Undeclared input files and solver versions are not seen.
