docs.title: Security audit: the PINNeAPPle web apps and their deployment
docs.text:
Scope: the FastAPI apps under apps/ (34 apps plus the static Playground and Zoo space), the shared glue apps/_shared/appkit.py and the library code it runs (pinneapple_core.service, the parsers and solvers the apps call), the Lab catalogue server (pinneapple_lab/server.py), and the deployment in apps/deploy (Docker Compose, Caddy, the app Dockerfiles). Reference: OWASP Top 10 (2021) and ASVS 4.0 levels 1–2. Audit date: 2026-10-18, commit ee4b770b (main).

Method: an inventory of every app's routes, uploads, process calls, deserialisation, path handling and outbound requests, read from the code (summarised below), plus the tools in the next section. Every finding marked measured was reproduced by a test or a scan; the others were read from the code and are marked as such.

docs.title: Tool results (baseline, before any change)
docs.text:
Tool Scope Result bandit 1.8 apps/, pinneapple_security/, pinneapple_core/service/ 24 findings: 2 high (B324 SHA-1, used for design IDs), 5 medium (3× B608 SQL built from a fixed list of ? placeholders, B610, B301 pickle of a server-written cache), 17 low semgrep 1.181 (semgrep-rules: python lang, fastapi, jwt, requests, cryptography, dockerfile) apps + the evaluators they call 241 findings: 52 error (32× dockerfile missing-user, 16 useless-inner-function, …), 116 warning (incl. 4× eval-detected, 2× avoid-pickle, 2× SHA-1), 73 info pip-audit 2.9 union of apps/*/requirements.txt, resolved to current releases 0 known vulnerabilities gitleaks 8.21 whole git history (502 commits) 39 hits, all false positives: the placeholder curl -u USER:PASSWORD in three app UIs and key="axial_compressor_stage_3d" in pinneapple_veriphysics/example_cases.py. No committed secret found hadolint 2.12 35 app Dockerfiles 37: 33× DL3013 (unpinned pip), 3× DL3008 (unpinned apt), 1 info trivy 0.69 config apps/ 33 high: DS-0002, image runs as root (all app Dockerfiles but the Simulation Runner and the GUI agent) trivy 0.69 image base images python:3.11-slim: 0 critical, 46 high (2 with a fix); caddy:2: 0 critical, 4 high; caddy:2.8.4-alpine (Playground): 7 critical, 86 high, 92 % fixable

Not run here: Trivy on the built app images. download.pytorch.org (the CPU torch wheel every app image installs) is blocked from this environment and the CUDA wheel from PyPI exceeded the disk; the base images and the resolved Python dependencies were scanned instead, and the Security workflow's weekly image job builds and scans one app image in CI.

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text:
Shared to every app (apps/_shared/appkit.py, before this change):

  • Login: optional HTTP Basic (<PREFIX>_USER / <PREFIX>_PASSWORD, plain text in the environment, constant-time compare); with neither set, every route is open. Any login is admin. No lockout, no rate limit.
  • Caller identity (job and upload ownership, monthly quotas): API key, else login, else ip: + the last X-Forwarded-For entry, believed from any peer.
  • Runtime (install_runtime): SQLite job queue (thread or process executor, optional time limit, no resource limits), API keys (random, stored as SHA-256, scopes stored but not enforced), usage metering, uploads (streamed size cap, name reduced to [A-Za-z0-9._-], suffix allow-list, stored under the data volume, not the web root).
  • Static files: /vendor (three.js), /studio, /shared, each app's /static. No security headers, no CORS middleware anywhere (browsers default to same-origin), no CSRF protection, no session cookies (Basic auth and X-API-Key only).
  • Errors: FastAPI's default 500 has no trace; many routes return f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" with 422; job logs carry the last 40 traceback lines to the job owner.

Per app (prefix · runtime · uploads · expensive work and its limit · process calls · deserialisation · outbound):

App Prefix Uploads (default limit) Expensive work, limit Notable aero_optimizer ADO none optimisation, GNN inference: BusyLimiter ADO_MAX_HEAVY; mesh exports unthrottled torch.load(weights_only=False) on the operator's ADO_MODEL path anomaly_detector ANOMALY csv/parquet/json via runtime (50 MB) analyses, benchmarks: job queue model JSON stored by Path(uri).name benchmark_arena ARN runtime (100 MB) arena runs: job queue, budget cap dataset constraints evaluated with eval calibration_lab CALIB tables via runtime job queue outbound link only (CALIB_IDENTIFIABILITY_URL, env) control_lab CONTROL json via runtime job queue — data_health EDH table (50 MB) BusyLimiter — data_standardizer EDS up to 8 files (80 MB) BusyLimiter — design_requirements UDR PDFs/docs (40 MB, 8 files) OCR (UDR_OCR_MAX_PAGES), local LLM via Ollama: BusyLimiter LLM output fills form fields only, runs nothing engineering_optimizer EDO runtime (20 MB) job queue external solvers only from the operator's EDO_SOLVERS (argv, no shell, timeout) evidence_report EVR files (200 MB) BusyLimiter report HTML escaped; urls are recorded, not fetched guiagent GUIAGENT workflow zip, self-hosted mode only (50 MB) FreeCAD/OpenFOAM runs: job queue zip checked per member; LLM picks among committed workflows heatsink_sizer HSS none BusyLimiter HSS_MAX_SIZING — identifiability_lab IDENT table (runtime cap) job queue, row/parameter caps — interop_hub IOP files/zips (500 MB) BusyLimiter zips via cae.upload.expand (count and size caps, no ratio, no name check); pickle of a server-written cache (sid.isalnum()) inverse_heat IHL none PINN training threads, IHL_MAX_JOBS jobs without owner (random 48-bit ids) inverse_studio INVS table job queue — mesh_quality MQA files/zips (200 MB) BusyLimiter zips via expand meshless_lab MESHLESS point cloud (20 MB) job queue, node and budget caps user formulas → sympy.sympify behind a string blacklist model_gateway MDL onnx/zip/json (100 MB) inference, metered surrogate zip → pickle.load, "sha256-checked" against a card in the same zip (admin only); remote refs: server fetches a user URL (admin only) model_lineage LIN files/zips (300 MB) BusyLimiter zips via expand observatory OBS none BusyLimiter for the heavy routes; /api/sky, /api/satellites unthrottled outbound to fixed hosts only; unbounded result cache pcb_hotspot PCB none BusyLimiter — physics_design PDO none job queue, evaluation caps — rom_lab ROM npz/zip/vtu/frd (200 MB) job queue np.load(allow_pickle=False) throughout; resolved-path check on job files sensitivity_lab SEN tables, onnx (50 MB) job queue; /api/design synchronous with unbounded n_sobol; ?wait= sleeps inside async handlers ONNX parsed by onnxruntime simulation_campaign CAMPAIGN tables, zip, inp, yaml (100 MB) job queue, 5000 cases base-case zip extractall without size limit; OpenFOAM edit file joined unchecked; user str.format templates simulation_comparator CMP files (300 MB) BusyLimiter whole upload read before the size check simulation_metadata SMD files (100 MB) BusyLimiter same simulation_preflight PFL files (200 MB) BusyLimiter same; gzipped OpenFOAM files decompressed without a cap simulation_runner RUNNER tables (20 MB) job queue, 60 cases Popen(argv) without shell; public mode runs 3 templates with range-checked numbers; RUNNER_SELF_HOSTED=1 runs any workflow by design surrogate_studio SUR tables (100 MB) job queue, budget cap pickled surrogate written and read by the server only twin_runtime TWIN tables, model JSON job queue live twins have no owner; MQTT/OPC-UA/DB URLs from the environment only uncertainty_lab UQL tables, onnx (50 MB) job queue; ?wait= in an async handler — validation_lab VAL files/zips (200 MB) BusyLimiter boundary-value formulas evaluated with eval; config paths may point outside the upload; os.chdir per run playground, zoo_space — static — Playground CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' and all of jsDelivr Lab catalogue (pinneapple_lab) LAB none (read-only) — own Basic auth, plain password, no lockout

Deployment (before): every image but two ran as root; no read_only, cap_drop, no-new-privileges or pids_limit in Compose; mem_limit set; healthchecks in the Dockerfiles; only Caddy published ports (80/443), the apps expose theirs; in existing-proxy mode the apps join the proxy network pinneapple_physai_net and the project network. Caddy: HSTS without subdomains, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, no Server header; body limits on 29 of 36 sites; no access log; TLS defaults. Secrets in .env (git-ignored; .env.example holds placeholders demo / change-me).

docs.title: Findings, ranked
docs.text: Severity follows OWASP risk rating (impact × likelihood) for the default deployment. "App PR", "Deploy PR" and "CI PR" are the pull requests that address them; tests are named so each claim can be re-run.

docs.title: Critical
docs.text: ID Finding OWASP / ASVS Status C1 Code execution through formula evaluation. pinneapple_data.audit (benchmark arena dataset constraints) and pinneapple_check.checks.results.evaluate_expr (Validation Lab boundary values from an uploaded config) ran user strings with eval(..., {"__builtins__": {}}), which attribute access escapes (().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()). Reachable without login when the app has none configured. Measured: before, constraint_mask("().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__().__len__() > 0", ...) returned True (the list of every loaded class was reached, the first step of the known escapes); after, it raises ExpressionError. The same for evaluate_expr. A03 Injection · V5.2.4 Fixed (App PR): both go through the existing AST interpreter pinneapple_data.contracts.expressions, never eval. Test test_constraint_and_boundary_evaluators_use_the_interpreter

docs.title: High
docs.text: ID Finding OWASP / ASVS Status H1 Arbitrary file overwrite in the Campaign Planner: openfoam_edits[].file is joined to the case directory without a check (../, absolute paths), then read, edited and written. Measured by test_openfoam_edit_outside_the_case_refused. A01 · V12.3.1 Fixed (App PR) H2 Caller spoofing via X-Forwarded-For when an app is reachable without the proxy (or from another container on the shared proxy network): the header chose the ip: principal, giving access to another anonymous caller's jobs and uploads and resetting quotas. Measured by test_forwarded_for_trusted_only_from_the_proxy. A01 · V4.1.3 Fixed (App PR): believed only from trusted proxies (loopback/private by default) H3 Pickle code execution in the Model Gateway: a surrogate model.zip is unpickled; its "sha256 check" compares the pickle with a hash from the same zip. Admin only. Measured by test_pickled_surrogate_upload_off_by_default_and_scanned. A08 · V5.5.3 Fixed (App PR): off unless MDL_ALLOW_PICKLE_UPLOAD=1, and then scanned for code-running globals first H4 Containers run as root (33 of 35 images; trivy DS-0002 ×33, semgrep missing-user ×32), with a writable root filesystem and all default capabilities. A05 · V14.1 Fixed (Deploy PR): uid 10001, read-only root, cap_drop: ALL, no-new-privileges, pids/CPU limits. Measured in a container (below) H5 No brute-force protection and plain-text passwords: unlimited Basic-auth attempts; passwords in plain text in the environment. A07 · V2.2.1, V2.4.1 Fixed (App PR): lockout per IP and user (429), scrypt/argon2id hashes (<PREFIX>_PASSWORD_HASH), audit events. Tests test_login_lockout_after_repeated_failures, test_hashed_and_legacy_plain_passwords

docs.title: Medium
docs.text: ID Finding Status M1 Cross-site request forgery: browsers resend cached Basic credentials, so a page elsewhere can POST to an app (start jobs, delete uploads, revoke keys). A01 · V4.2.2 Fixed (App PR): Fetch-Metadata/Origin check on state-changing requests, test_cross_site_post_refused M2 No security headers from the apps (CSP, frame-ancestors, Permissions-Policy). A05 · V14.4 Fixed (App PR): CSP with hashes of each app's own inline scripts (no script 'unsafe-inline'), checked against every app page by test_app_pages_fit_their_csp M3 Zip bombs and unbounded decompression: Campaign extractall without limits (and the case copied ~51 times), cae.upload.expand without a counted size or member-name check, gzip without a cap. A05 · V12.1.2 Fixed (App PR): pinneapple_security.archives (names, links, counted sizes, ratio), gunzip cap M4 No per-caller rate limits on expensive routes (only per-worker concurrency). A04 · V11.1.4 Fixed (App PR): token buckets per caller, 429 + Retry-After M5 SSRF: the gateway calls the URL of a remote ModelRef (admin only), including loopback and the cloud metadata address. Measured: before, publishing a ref to a service on 127.0.0.1 made the server send it a request; after, none. A10 · V12.6.1 Fixed (App PR): check_outbound_url with MDL_REMOTE_ALLOW_HOSTS M6 Validation Lab: config result/reference paths may point outside the upload (server files into the report). A01 · V12.3.1 Fixed (App PR), test_validation_lab_config_confined_to_uploads M7 Denial of service: ?wait= sleeps inside async handlers (Sensitivity, Uncertainty); Sensitivity /api/design synchronous with unbounded n_sobol; Observatory cache unbounded; jobs without resource limits and orphaned grandchildren on kill. A04 Fixed (App PR): threadpool, caps, bounded cache, opt-in setrlimit, process-group kill (test_job_limits_and_no_traceback_in_job_log) M8 User str.format templates in the Campaign Planner (attribute access, gigabyte padding); integer ** in its formula evaluator. A03 Fixed (App PR), test_template_fields_restricted M9 Meshless formulas reach sympy.sympify (which uses eval) behind a string blacklist. A03 Fixed (App PR): grammar check first M10 Playground base image caddy:2.8.4-alpine: 7 critical, 86 high CVEs (trivy). A06 Fixed (Deploy PR): caddy:2-alpine by digest, 0 critical / 4 high M11 Twin Runtime: live twins have no owner; anyone allowed in can stop, fault or feed another user's twin. A01 Open: set a login or TWIN_REQUIRE_API_KEY=1 on a shared server; ownership per twin needs a product decision M12 Comparator, Metadata, Preflight, Validation Lab, Twin models read a whole upload before their size check. A04 Mitigated: request body counted and capped by the app (<PREFIX>_MAX_BODY_MB, 600 MB) and per site by Caddy (Deploy PR); a per-app streaming cap is open

docs.title: Low
docs.text:
ID Finding Status L1 Exception type and message in 422 answers; tracebacks in job logs (FastAPI's default 500 already had none). A09 · V7.4.1 Partly fixed: JSON 500 with a reference id (test_no_stack_trace_to_clients); job tracebacks go to the server log unless <PREFIX>_JOB_TRACEBACKS=1. Input-error messages stay (they explain the input) L2 API key scopes are stored but not enforced; any login is admin. A01 Partly: <PREFIX>_ADMIN_USERS (App PR). Scopes open L3 Validation Lab os.chdir races between concurrent runs. Fixed (App PR): serialised L4 Inverse Heat jobs have no owner (random 48-bit ids). Accepted (no uploads, demo results) L5 A ModelRef zoo:<name> bypasses the app's zoo allow-list in Sensitivity/Uncertainty (weights load with weights_only=True). Open L6 HDF5 inputs read with h5py [()]: compression bombs and external links not checked. Open (needs a test with crafted files) L7 Unpinned Python dependencies (DL3013 ×33) and base images by tag. A06 Partly (CI PR): Dependabot, weekly pip-audit and Trivy, Caddy by digest. Hash-pinned requirements were not generated: the CPU torch index is unreachable from the audit environment L8 RUNNER_SELF_HOSTED=1 runs any workflow (commands, Docker, sbatch) by design. Documented: only behind its own login L9 bandit B324: SHA-1 for design IDs in apps/aero_optimizer/tools. Fixed (CI PR): usedforsecurity=False (same IDs) L10 LLM use (Design Requirements, GUI agent): model output fills fields or picks one of the committed workflows; nothing it writes is executed. Prompt injection can at most pick another committed workflow. A03 (LLM01) Accepted L11 Lab catalogue: plain-text password, no lockout. Fixed (App PR): LAB_PASSWORD_HASH, lockout

Checked and not exploitable: the gateway's zoo: reference with a path (../../etc/passwd): pp.zoo.load only accepts registered names (measured: KeyError). Uploads: names are reduced to a safe basename and stored under the data volume by a random id (test_upload_name_traversal_and_suffix). ROM Lab and Physics Design job files: allow-listed or resolved-path checked. np.load everywhere with allow_pickle=False. No committed secrets (gitleaks, whole history). Not applicable: session cookies (none are set; Basic auth and API keys only).

Not implemented: OIDC/OAuth for browser logins. Recommended route: an identity-aware proxy in front of Caddy's sites (forward_auth to oauth2-proxy or Authelia), keeping X-API-Key for API clients.

docs.title: After the changes (measured)
docs.text:
The same behaviour probe (15 properties, FastAPI TestClient against appkit and the real Campaign Planner and Model Gateway apps, plus the library evaluators) was run unchanged on main and on the changed tree:

Property main changed security headers (CSP with frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff) fail pass no stack trace or exception text in a 500 pass (FastAPI default) pass (+ reference id) no CORS grant to a foreign origin pass pass oversized request body → 413 (1 MB limit, 3 MB body) fail (200) pass upload name ../../x.csv neutralised pass pass rate limit → 429 (5/min, 8 POSTs) fail (8× 200) pass (5× 200, 3× 429) lockout after repeated failed logins, also for the right password fail (401 then 200) pass (429) hashed password (PASSWORD_HASH) fail (unsupported) pass cross-site POST refused fail (200) pass (403) direct client cannot choose its identity with X-Forwarded-For fail pass dataset constraint cannot reach Python internals fail pass boundary-value formula cannot reach Python internals fail pass Campaign edit cannot write outside the case fail (file modified) pass (job refused, file untouched) gateway does not call an internal address fail (1 request) pass (0) CAE upload refuses .. member names fail pass total 3 / 15 15 / 15

Tools:

Check Before After bandit (same scope) 2 high, 5 medium, 17 low 0 high, 5 medium, 19 low semgrep (same rules, same scope) 52 error / 116 warning / 73 info 21 error / 113 warning / 72 info (missing-user 32 → 0, eval-detected 4 → 0) trivy config 33 high (DS-0002) 0 hadolint 36 warnings, 1 info 36 warnings, 1 info (unpinned pip/apt: L7) gitleaks (history, with .gitleaks.toml allow-listing the 3 placeholders) 39 false positives 0 trivy, Playground base image 7 critical / 86 high 0 critical / 4 high A hardened container (uid, capabilities, writes) root, all default capabilities, writable root uid 10001, CapEff 0, NoNewPrivs 1, / and /srv read-only, /data and /tmp writable

The remaining semgrep errors are code-quality rules (useless-inner-function for FastAPI route closures, identical-is-comparison in two scripts), not security findings; the medium bandit findings are B608 on SQL built only from ? placeholders, B610 and the server-written interop cache (L-level, reviewed above).

docs.title: Operator runbook: PINNeAPPle apps
docs.text: Commands run in apps/deploy on the server unless stated. <PREFIX> is the app's prefix (HSS, MDL, CAMPAIGN, ...; the list is in .env.example), <svc> its Compose service (heatsink, models, campaign, ...). Settings are described in apps/_shared/README.md and the host in docs/security/server.md.

docs.title: Upgrade to the hardened containers (once)
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] The first upgrade to the non-root images (PR "Harden the deployment") needs a one-time ownership change of the app volumes, before the new images start; otherwise apps that keep state on a volume can not write to it.

cd apps/deploy
docker compose down
for v in $(docker volume ls -q | grep -E '^pinneapple-apps_(.*_data|obs_cache)$' | grep -v caddy_data); do
  docker run --rm -v "$v":/v alpine chown -R 10001:0 /v
done
docker compose build --pull && docker compose up -d
sudo ./check_server.sh                     # then every service healthy in `docker compose ps`

Also set login hashes (<PREFIX>_PASSWORD_HASH, below) and, if the Model Gateway hosted pickled Surrogate Studio models, decide on MDL_ALLOW_PICKLE_UPLOAD (off by default now).

docs.title: Rotate credentials
docs.text:
An app login password

python -m pinneapple_security hash-password            # prompts twice, prints $scrypt$... (or $argon2id$...)

Put the hash in .env as <PREFIX>_PASSWORD_HASH=..., writing each $ as $$, and clear <PREFIX>_PASSWORD. Then docker compose up -d <svc>: the container is recreated with the new value and the old password stops working.

An admin token (<PREFIX>_ADMIN_TOKEN): generate one with python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))", put it in .env, run docker compose up -d <svc>, and update every client that uses it.

API keys (callers of /api and /v1):

curl -s -H "X-Admin-Token: $TOKEN" https://<host>/api/keys                    # list: id, name, created, revoked
curl -s -X POST -H "X-Admin-Token: $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name": "ci-2026-10"}' https://<host>/api/keys                       # new key, shown once
curl -s -X DELETE -H "X-Admin-Token: $TOKEN" https://<host>/api/keys/<id>       # revoke the old one

Keys are stored as SHA-256 digests. A revoked key gets 401 at once, in every worker.

The audit HMAC key (<PREFIX>_AUDIT_KEY): a new key starts a new chain. Move the old audit.jsonl aside first (docker compose exec <svc> mv /data/<prefix>/audit.jsonl /data/<prefix>/audit-<date>.jsonl), keep the old key with that archive so it can still be verified, then set the new key and recreate the container.

A credential found in the repository or a log: treat it as public. Rotate it as above, revoke what it unlocks, and check the audit trail and access log for its use since it was exposed.

docs.title: Add or remove a user
docs.text:
Single login per app: <PREFIX>_USER + <PREFIX>_PASSWORD_HASH. Several logins: a users file, mounted read-only.

mkdir -p secrets && chmod 700 secrets
printf 'ana:%s\n' "$(python -m pinneapple_security hash-password)" >> secrets/models.users
chmod 600 secrets/models.users

In docker-compose.yml (or an override file) for the service:

    environment:
      MDL_USERS_FILE: /run/secrets/users
      MDL_ADMIN_USERS: ana                 # who may manage keys and publish models
    volumes:
      - ./secrets/models.users:/run/secrets/users:ro

docker compose up -d models. To remove someone, delete their line and recreate the container. The container runs as uid 10001: make the file readable to it (chown 10001 secrets/models.users).

A user is locked out after too many failed logins (429 with Retry-After): the lock ends by itself after <PREFIX>_LOGIN_LOCK_S (15 minutes), or at once with docker compose restart <svc> (lock state is in memory). If fail2ban banned the address: fail2ban-client set pinneapple-apps unbanip <ip> (or pinneapple-caddy).

docs.title: Read the audit log
docs.text:
Each auth or admin event is one JSON line on the container's stderr and, when the app has a data directory, one record in a hash-chained trail:

docker compose logs --no-log-prefix <svc> | grep '"event"' | jq -c 'select(.outcome != "ok")'
docker compose exec <svc> python - <<'EOF'
from pinneapple_security.audit import AuditLog
log = AuditLog("/data/<prefix>/audit.jsonl")
print(log.verify())                                        # {'ok': True, 'n': ..., 'head': ...}
for r in log.query(action="login_failed")[-20:]:
    print(r["time"], r["actor"], r["data"].get("ip"), r["target"])
EOF

Events: login_failed, login_locked, csrf_blocked, rate_limited, api_key_lockout, admin_denied, api_key_created, api_key_revoked. verify() names the first record that was changed, removed or reordered. The Caddy access log (/data/access.log in the caddy_data volume) has every request with its status; secrets in headers are redacted by Caddy.

docs.title: Respond to an incident
docs.text:
1. Contain. Ban the source (fail2ban-client set pinneapple-caddy banip <ip>), or take the app off line (docker compose stop <svc>). For a suspected compromise of a container, stop it but do not remove it.
  2. Preserve evidence before changing anything: 
    ts=$(date +%F-%H%M); mkdir -p /root/incident-$ts
docker compose logs --timestamps > /root/incident-$ts/compose.log
docker inspect $(docker compose ps -q) > /root/incident-$ts/inspect.json
docker run --rm -v pinneapple-apps_<svc>_data:/v:ro -v /root/incident-$ts:/out alpine tar czf /out/data.tgz -C /v .
cp /var/lib/docker/volumes/pinneapple-apps_caddy_data/_data/access.log* /root/incident-$ts/
  3. Assess. Verify the audit trails (above), list API keys and admin events, compare running images with the built ones (docker compose images), and check docker diff <container> (should be empty: read-only root).
  4. Eradicate and recover. Rotate every credential of the affected app (and shared ones), revoke all its API keys, rebuild from a clean checkout (docker compose build --pull --no-cache <svc>), restore data from the last backup taken before the incident if it was altered, and start again.
  5. Follow up. Write down the timeline, the cause and the fix; report vulnerabilities in PINNeAPPle itself as described in SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Update dependencies
docs.text:
• Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) opens weekly pull requests for Python packages, the Docker base images (pinned by digest where pinned) and GitHub Actions. The Security workflow runs on each: bandit, pip-audit, gitleaks, hadolint, Trivy on the base images, the security tests and a CycloneDX SBOM.
  • On the server, after merging: git pull && docker compose build --pull && docker compose up -d, then sudo ./check_server.sh and a look at docker compose ps (every service healthy).
  • A published vulnerability in a dependency: pip-audit -r <(docker compose exec -T <svc> pip freeze) shows whether an image is affected; raise the floor in pyproject.toml or the app's requirements.txt, rebuild, redeploy.
  • SBOM of an image: the Security workflow uploads sbom-*.cdx.json artifacts; locally, docker compose exec <svc> python -m pinneapple_security sbom -o /tmp/sbom.json.

docs.title: Server hardening: the host that runs the PINNeAPPle apps
docs.text:
The apps run as Docker containers (apps/deploy/docker-compose.yml) behind one Caddy: either the project's own (ports 80/443 on the host) or an existing Caddy on a shared Docker network (docker-compose.existing-proxy.yml, e.g. PROXY_NETWORK=pinneapple_physai_net). This page covers what the repository configures and what the operator sets up on the host. apps/deploy/check_server.sh checks the host part read-only and prints PASS / WARN / FAIL.

internet ─▶ 80/443 ─▶ Caddy (TLS, headers, body limits, access log) ─▶ app containers (no host ports)
                         │                                                  │
                    fail2ban (DOCKER-USER chain) ◀── access log + app auth events (docker logs)

docs.title: What the repository sets
docs.text:
Layer Setting Where Image runs as uid 10001 (USER 10001:0), HOME=/tmp, /data owned by that user every apps/*/Dockerfile, pinneapple_lab/deploy/Dockerfile Container read_only: true root filesystem, /tmp as tmpfs, cap_drop: [ALL], no-new-privileges, pids_limit, cpus, mem_limit, rotated json-file logs x-app-hardening in apps/deploy/docker-compose.yml Network only Caddy publishes ports; the apps expose theirs on the Compose network (and on the proxy network in existing-proxy mode) docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.existing-proxy.yml Proxy TLS 1.2/1.3, HSTS, nosniff, frame and referrer policy, Permissions-Policy, no Server header, a request body limit on every site, rotated JSON access log apps/deploy/Caddyfile ((common) snippet) App CSP, rate limits, login lockout, hashed passwords, CSRF origin check, body limit, audit trail pinneapple_security.web via apps/_shared/appkit.py (see apps/_shared/README.md)

The GUI agent (FreeCAD/X11) and Ollama keep a writable root filesystem (x-base-hardening): their images write outside /data and /tmp. Everything else is read-only.

docs.title: Upgrading a server whose volumes were written by root (run once, before starting the new images)
docs.text:
Before this change the containers ran as root, so existing named volumes hold root-owned files that uid 10001 can not write. Once, before starting the new images:

cd apps/deploy
docker compose down
for v in $(docker volume ls -q | grep -E '^pinneapple-apps_(.*_data|obs_cache)$' | grep -v caddy_data); do
  docker run --rm -v "$v":/v alpine chown -R 10001:0 /v
done

The Caddy volumes (caddy_data, caddy_config) stay as they are: the official Caddy image runs as root, with only NET_BIND_SERVICE.

docs.title: 1. SSH: keys only
docs.text:
/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-hardening.conf:

PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin prohibit-password
PubkeyAuthentication yes
MaxAuthTries 3
X11Forwarding no
AllowAgentForwarding no

Then sshd -t && systemctl reload ssh. Keep a second session open until a new login with the key works.

docs.title: 2. Firewall: SSH, 80 and 443 only
docs.text:
ufw default deny incoming
ufw default allow outgoing
ufw allow 22/tcp            # or your SSH port
ufw allow 80/tcp
ufw allow 443/tcp
ufw allow 443/udp           # HTTP/3
ufw enable

Docker publishes ports through its own iptables chains, before ufw sees the packets: a container started with -p 8080:8080 is reachable from the internet whatever ufw says. That is why only Caddy publishes ports; the check script fails on any other container with a published port. fail2ban bans go into the DOCKER-USER chain, which Docker evaluates first, so a ban also reaches the Caddy container.

docs.title: 3. fail2ban for SSH, Caddy and the app logins
docs.text:
apt install fail2ban
cp apps/deploy/fail2ban/filter.d/*.conf /etc/fail2ban/filter.d/
cp apps/deploy/fail2ban/jail.d/pinneapple.local /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/
fail2ban-regex /var/lib/docker/volumes/pinneapple-apps_caddy_data/_data/access.log pinneapple-caddy
systemctl restart fail2ban && fail2ban-client status
  • pinneapple-caddy: 20 answers 401/429 to one client IP in 10 minutes ban it for an hour (Caddy's JSON access log; for an existing proxy, set logpath to its log).
  • pinneapple-apps: 10 failed logins, lockouts, refused cross-site posts or invalid API keys logged by the apps (docker logs, one JSON line per event).
  • sshd: 4 failures in 10 minutes.

The apps lock a client out on their own as well (<PREFIX>_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES, default 10 in 15 minutes); fail2ban takes the client off the network for every app at once.

docs.title: 4. Automatic security updates
docs.text:
apt install unattended-upgrades
dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades      # writes /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades

Reboot when /var/run/reboot-required exists (the check script warns). Images: rebuild weekly (docker compose build --pull && docker compose up -d) so the Debian and Caddy base images bring their fixes; the CI job security.yml scans the base images with Trivy.

docs.title: 5. Docker daemon
docs.text:
/etc/docker/daemon.json:

{
  "no-new-privileges": true,
  "live-restore": true,
  "icc": false,
  "userland-proxy": false,
  "log-driver": "json-file",
  "log-opts": {"max-size": "10m", "max-file": "5"}
}

systemctl restart docker (with live-restore the containers keep running). The socket /var/run/docker.sock is root-equivalent: never mount it into an app container, and keep the docker group empty except for administrators. User-namespace remapping ("userns-remap": "default") adds another layer but changes volume ownership; turn it on only for a fresh server.

docs.title: 6. Caddy
docs.text:
The project's Caddyfile already sets TLS, headers, limits and logs. For an existing Caddy on pinneapple_physai_net, add the same snippet to its Caddyfile and import it in each PINNeAPPle site:

(pinneapple) {
    encode zstd gzip
    tls {
        protocols tls1.2 tls1.3
    }
    header {
        Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
        X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
        X-Frame-Options "DENY"
        Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
        Permissions-Policy "camera=(), microphone=(), payment=(), usb=(), geolocation=(self)"
        -Server
    }
    log {
        output file /data/access.log {
            roll_size 50MiB
            roll_keep 10
        }
        format json
    }
}

heatsink.example.org {
    import pinneapple
    request_body {
        max_size 1MB
    }
    reverse_proxy pinneapple-heatsink:8080
}

The body limit per app is in apps/deploy/Caddyfile. Optional: a login at the proxy in front of an app that has none of its own, with a bcrypt hash from caddy hash-password:

    basic_auth {
        demo $2a$14$...
    }

Rate limiting at the proxy needs a Caddy built with a rate-limit module (e.g. xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit); the stock image has none. The apps enforce their own limits (<PREFIX>_RATE_LIMIT), per worker process.

docs.title: 7. Secrets
docs.text:
• .env holds the logins and tokens: chmod 600 apps/deploy/.env, owned by root, never committed (apps/deploy/.gitignore). .env.example is the template and holds placeholders only.
  • Store password hashes (<PREFIX>_PASSWORD_HASH, python -m pinneapple_security hash-password), not passwords. In .env, write every $ of a hash as $$.
  • Admin tokens (<PREFIX>_ADMIN_TOKEN) and the audit HMAC key (<PREFIX>_AUDIT_KEY): 32+ random bytes, python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))".
  • Rotation: docs/security/runbook.md.

docs.title: 8. Backups and a restore test
docs.text:
What holds state: the named volumes pinneapple-apps_*_data (jobs, uploads, API keys, usage, audit trails), pinneapple-apps_obs_cache, pinneapple-apps_caddy_data (certificates, access log) and apps/deploy/.env.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# /usr/local/sbin/pinneapple-backup, daily from a systemd timer or cron
set -euo pipefail
dest=/var/backups/pinneapple/$(date +%F)
mkdir -p "$dest"
for v in $(docker volume ls -q | grep '^pinneapple-apps_'); do
  docker run --rm -v "$v":/v:ro -v "$dest":/out alpine tar czf "/out/$v.tgz" -C /v .
done
install -m 600 /srv/pinneapple/apps/deploy/.env "$dest/env"
find /var/backups/pinneapple -maxdepth 1 -type d -mtime +14 -exec rm -rf {} +
touch /var/backups/pinneapple/last-ok           # read by check_server.sh

Copy the backups off the server (restic, borg or rclone to object storage, encrypted). Restore test, once a quarter on a scratch VM: restore one _data volume, start that app, open a job from before the backup, and check the audit trail (python -c "from pinneapple_security.audit import AuditLog; print(AuditLog('audit.jsonl').verify())" must report 'ok': True).

docs.title: 9. Log retention
docs.text: Log Retention Setting Container stdout/stderr (app auth events) 5 × 10 MB per container compose logging, daemon.json Caddy access log 10 × 50 MB, at most 30 days Caddyfile roll_keep, roll_keep_for systemd journal (SSH, fail2ban) SystemMaxUse=1G, MaxRetentionSec=90day /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/retention.conf App audit trails kept with the volume; archive yearly audit.jsonl in each app's data directory

docs.title: 10. Check
docs.text:
sudo apps/deploy/check_server.sh

It reads sshd's effective settings (sshd -T), ufw/nftables, listening ports, fail2ban jails, unattended upgrades, NTP, journald, daemon.json, every running app container (user, read-only root, capabilities, no-new-privileges, published ports) and the backup stamp, and changes nothing. Exit code 1 when a check fails.

docs.title: Physics AI Strategy — structure and first implementation
docs.text:
Status: structured from the owner's research (October 2026), which covers the public PINNeAPPle repository, recent Physics AI / Scientific ML / CAE job postings, and public moves by NVIDIA, Siemens, Dassault, SimScale, PhysicsX, PTC, Blue Origin, Periodic Labs and Engineering AI startups.

Verification status: this document does not verify the market facts quoted in the research (company launches, customer counts, dataset sizes, pricing, marketing claims). Treat them as working hypotheses until checked against primary sources.

Scope of this file: what the research recommends, how that maps to the code that exists today, what is implemented, and what is decided versus still open.

docs.title: 1. Thesis
docs.text:
Physics AI is moving from a question of neural architecture ("which network solves this PDE best?") to a question of engineering infrastructure. Commercial value shifts from the model to the accelerated workflow: explore more designs, turn hours of simulation into seconds of prediction, operate a digital twin, and let an agent run the engineering process.

Evolution proposed by the research:

Solver → Surrogate → Physics AI → Design AI → Digital Twin → Engineering Agent → Autonomous Engineering

Recommended positioning: an open, vendor-neutral infrastructure layer between physical models and engineering applications. PINNeAPPle does not replace solvers (OpenFOAM, FEniCS, Ansys, Siemens). It sits above them and composes them.

Recommended one-line description:

An open, vendor-neutral infrastructure for building, validating and deploying AI systems for physical engineering.

docs.title: 2. Current state of the repository
docs.text:
Verified by inspecting module directories and ROADMAP.md on main (October 2026). "Exists" means a module is present, not that it is validated in production.

Layer Modules present Main gap Problem specification pinneapple_problemdesign (ProblemSpec for elicited problems), pinneapple_physics/pde_environment (ProblemSpec for PDEs), pinneapple_data/upd_types (ConditionSpec) Three overlapping specs; no single universal physical problem (see §5, Decision D1). Physics AI models pinneapple_neural, pinneapple_models, pinneapple_physics (PINN, neural operators, GNN, ROM, SINDy, symplectic models) No common interface; the user chooses the architecture. Physics engines pinneapple_solvers, pinneapple_simulation; bridges to OpenFOAM and FEniCS in the CFD product Bridges are per product, not a common backend contract. Geometry SDF, CSG, mesh and GNN code No geometry as a first-class layer. Data pinneapple_data, pinneapple_registry (problem, dataset, model, experiment stores), pinneapple_pdb Stores exist separately; no lineage graph linking them. Trust and validation pinneapple_analysis/trust/trust_gate.py (OOD, residual, ensemble per prediction); pinneapple_analysis/verification/evidence_graph.py; pinneapple_hub/model_card.py No deployment decision aggregating the checks (addressed in §4). Optimization Bayesian optimization code and design modules (pinneapple_design) Not connected to surrogate validation. Agents pinneapple_llm (guardrails), pinneapple_tools, pinneapple_problemdesign No agent that runs the full workflow through the platform APIs. Benchmarking pinneapple_arena, benchmarks/ Not yet a reference benchmark with domain-of-validity reporting. Foundation / world models pinneapple_worldmodel (described as generalist) No multi-domain demonstration against baselines.

docs.title: 3. The research's diagnosis: nine problems, one architecture
docs.text:
The research lists twenty problems. The ones that drive the plan:

  1. CAD / engineering intent → executable simulation. Missing: an engineering problem compiler (intent → physics → geometry → mesh → solver → surrogate → validation).
  2. Generating data efficiently. Missing: a simulation factory (CAD → design of experiments → solver → dataset → quality control), with active learning to pick the next simulations.
  3. Choosing the right model. Missing: a model selector that compares candidates (PINN, operator, GNN, ROM) on a benchmark, instead of a fixed choice.
  4. Out-of-distribution generalization. Missing: a generalization suite that tests geometry, physics, resolution and regime OOD separately.
  5. Knowing when to trust a surrogate. Missing: a trust layer that combines residual checks, OOD, uncertainty and boundary-condition violations into a decision.
  6. Deciding AI versus solver per request. Missing: an adaptive fidelity engine.
  7. Surrogate, solver and optimizer are separate systems. Missing: a design loop (requirements → candidates → physics AI → high-fidelity validation → Pareto front → engineer review).
  8. Generated geometry ignores physics. Missing: a physics-aware generator.
  9. Engineering language is not executable. Missing: intent → physics selection → geometry → material → boundary conditions.
  10. Agents cannot call engineering tools safely. Missing: a typed, auditable tool surface.
  11. Simulations are not reproducible. Missing: experiment lineage (commit, environment, data, seeds, hardware, outputs).
  12. Multi-fidelity learning. Missing: training on cheap, medium and high-fidelity data together.
  13. Transfer across geometries and applications.
  14. Neural operator scaling.
  15. Physics AI on bad problems (stiff, multi-scale, sparse data).
  16. Connecting the physical world to the model (sensors, state estimation).
  17. Multi-objective optimization.
  18. Explaining model decisions to engineers.
  19. Connecting multiple solvers.
  20. No universal representation of a physical problem.

Priority list from the research (ten problems, in order): engineering intent → simulation (1); simulation data factory (2); model selector (3); OOD generalization (4); trust layer (5); adaptive fidelity (6); design loop (7); orchestrator (8); runtime and digital twin (9); universal physical problem (10). Foundation models and world models come after these.

docs.title: 4. Products the research proposes (seven internal products)
docs.text:
Internal product Pipeline Existing base Status Problem Compiler natural language or CAD → universal physical problem problemdesign, physics/pde_environment Specification gap (D1). Simulation Factory CAD → DOE → solver → dataset → quality control simulation, data, CFD product pipeline Works per product; not generalized. Physics Model Factory dataset → architecture search → training → UQ → benchmark → registry neural, train, registry, arena Pieces exist; no single pipeline. Physics Trust prediction → physics checks → OOD → UQ → validation → trust score analysis/trust, hub/model_card First slice implemented (§5). Design Explorer requirements → generate → simulate → surrogate → optimize → Pareto design, analysis Not connected to validation. Physics Agent engineer ↔ agent ↔ CAD / solver / model / optimizer llm, tools Not built. Physics Runtime trained model → API → edge → digital twin → sensor stream → continuous validation systems/digital_twin, hub Partial.

The research also proposes Geometric AI (CAD, B-Rep, SDF, point cloud, mesh and graph representations) and Multi-fidelity learning as cross-cutting capabilities.

docs.title: 5.1 Done: deployment trust report (Physics Trust, first slice)
docs.text:
pinneapple_analysis/trust/trust_report.py combines independent checks into one decision: APPROVED, REVIEW or REJECT.

  • Check: one check with status supports, contradicts or not_run, criticality, weight and reason. The vocabulary matches the proofs used by the CFD product's verification module.
  • TrustReport: score (weighted over executed checks), coverage, reasons, Markdown and dict output.
  • from_trust_score: converts the sub-scores of the existing TrustGate (OOD, PDE residual, ensemble) into checks.

Decision rules (design choices, not standards): - any failed critical check → REJECT; - any other failed check → REVIEW; - coverage below 60% → REVIEW; - score below 0.80 → REVIEW; - otherwise → APPROVED.

Tests: tests/test_trust_report.py (9 tests) and tests/test_trust_gate.py pass.

docs.title: 5.2 Decided, not yet implemented
docs.text:
• D1 — Universal physical problem. Do not add a third specification class. First reconcile problemdesign.ProblemSpec, physics.pde_environment.ProblemSpec and upd_types.ConditionSpec into one representation with explicit conversions, then add the universal problem as a façade over it. Reason: a third class increases fragmentation, which is the problem the research describes.
  • D2 — Trust report is linked to model records. Next step: store the TrustReport in ModelCard and in the registry, so every published model carries its decision and reasons.
  • D3 — Calibrate trust limits. The 0.80 score, 60% coverage and 0.7 sub-score limits are provisional. Calibrate them on the existing surrogates of the CFD product, whose measured errors range from 0.23% to about 10%.

docs.title: 6. Demonstrations the research recommends
docs.text:
Five demonstrations, each chosen to show the full loop rather than a single model:

  1. Aerospace: wing geometry (STEP) → CFD → neural operator → drag/lift prediction → geometry optimization → high-fidelity CFD validation.
  2. Automotive: vehicle geometry → simulation factory (about 10,000 designs) → neural operator → OOD validation → aerodynamic optimization.
  3. Structural: bracket → FEA → surrogate → stress prediction → mass optimization → uncertainty → validation.
  4. Industrial digital twin: CFD/FEA → surrogate → sensor stream → ensemble Kalman filter → anomaly detection → prediction.
  5. Agentic engineering (flagship): "Design a cooling system that keeps the electronics below 80 °C while minimizing mass and pressure drop" → the system interprets the problem, generates geometry, selects physics, runs simulations, trains a surrogate, optimizes, validates, and returns five candidate designs.

The CFD product (pipe erosion) is a vertical slice of demonstration 1's pattern and should be the reference for the surrogate and trust pieces.

docs.title: 7. Phases
docs.text:
Phase Focus Entry condition 1 Universal physical problem (D1) — 2 Simulation factory Phase 1 3 Physics model factory Phase 2 4 Trust, OOD and validation (§5.1, D2, D3) Phase 3 5 Adaptive fidelity Phase 4 6 Design optimization Phase 5 7 Engineering agent Phases 1–6 provide APIs for the agent 8 Digital twin runtime Phase 4 (trust) and phase 6 9 Foundation and world models Phases 1–8

The research's rule for the sequence: each stage feeds the next, forming a closed loop — problem → data → model → trust → decision → optimization → deployment → real world → more data.

Recommendation from the research: temporarily freeze horizontal expansion of models, and invest in the sequence above. The repository already contains most primitives; the work is composition, not new architectures.

docs.title: 8. What the research recommends not doing
docs.text:
• Do not add more architectures without an industrial problem that needs them.
  • Do not try to build a new general-purpose solver or a new CAE platform.
  • Do not compete head-on with SimScale on CFD/FEA.
  • Do not build a generic "ChatGPT for CFD": it is easy to copy.

docs.title: 9. Decisions the owner must take
docs.text:
These are not decided here:

  • Whether the product is sold as a platform, as engineering applications, or as both.
  • The first industrial vertical (the research points at aerospace and automotive; the current product is pipe erosion).
  • Whether to publish a reference architecture or keep the design internal until the first demonstration exists.
  • The trust limits (D3) and the erosion accuracy target for the CFD product (today only ΔP has a target).

docs.title: 10. Caveats
docs.text:
• Market and company statements in the research are not verified here (see the status note at the top).
  • The research text is long and was partly duplicated in the source file; this document keeps only the structure, not every example.
  • Career-related remarks in the source research are intentionally not part of this repository document.
